key_insight: ST2M uses crystal symmetry to guide generation, achieving 96.37% structural validity while improving the yield of stable, unique, and novel candidates.
engineering_relevance: Generating candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints could accelerate materials screening and reduce wasted downstream calculations.
method: Represent crystals as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits.
Condition discrete–continuous diffusion on Wyckoff patterns and apply degree-of-freedom masks.
Use a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables.
evidence_signal: For known dataset patterns, 23.86% of generated structures met stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria—a 68.15% relative improvement over the best baseline—and first-principles calculations identified 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected low-predicted-energy candidates.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify performance on unknown Wyckoff patterns, and first-principles validation covers only selected candidates.
paper_title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
